insights.title: More — 2 more point(s) not shown here — see the tables below.
insights.body: ### Total — by app (country = All · OS = iOS)

android.head: Expect App Total Revenue to weaken in about 7 days — fewer of the people installing are subscribing.
android.body: App Total New Subs is -0.6% while App Total Install is +369.5% — fewer of the people who installed are subscribing (-370.1pp less growth). New subs start as 7-day free trials, so today's new subs are next period's App Total Revenue. So expect App Total Revenue to weaken in about 7 days. App Total Revenue is +0.0% right now, so expect that to cool off.

android.head: App Total Revenue +0.0% does not match new subs -34.5% from 7 days earlier — this growth is not coming from new customers.
android.body: App Total Revenue this week vs last week is +0.0%, but App Total New Subs last week vs the week before was -34.5% — they moved in opposite directions. Most new subs start as a 7-day free trial, so the revenue landing now mostly comes from people who subscribed about 7 days ago. Since those subs went the other way, this growth is coming from existing customers instead: check renewals and cancellations, refunds, or a recent price change — not marketing or installs.

android.head: App Total Install is moving faster than the other steps (+369.5% vs about -0.6%).
android.body: App Total Install is +369.5% while the other steps are all moving about -0.6% — a gap of +370.1pp. When one step moves very differently from the rest, the cause is usually specific to that step.

ios.head: Where installs come from is shifting away from SEO Install (-23.0% vs -0.6% for installs overall).
ios.body: SEO Install was 12,141, -23.0% against last week, while total installs moved -0.6% — a difference of -22.4 percentage points. SEO Install is now 5.7% of all installs, so the balance between channels is moving away from it; free traffic slipping while paid holds up means we are buying more of the same installs..

ios.head: US is out of line with every other country on App Total New Subs (+6.0% vs -1.9%).

ios.head: App Total Revenue -5.5% matches the new subs signed up 7 days earlier.
ios.body: App Total Revenue this week vs last week is -5.5%, and App Total New Subs last week vs the week before was -4.4% — both moved the same way. Most new subs start as a 7-day free trial, so the revenue landing now mostly comes from people who subscribed about 7 days ago. This is the normal pattern, so no surprise is building up.

ios.head: Every app is turning installs into New Subs at its usual rate.
ios.body: In every app, New Subs is growing at about the same rate as Install (within 5 percentage points), so no app is unusually good or bad at turning installs into subscribers right now.

ios.head: GB turns installs into new subs best of anywhere (22.1% vs 12.2% overall).
ios.body: In GB, 22.1% of installs turn into new subs, versus 12.2% across all markets and apps (+9.9pp difference). That is much better than the rest — worth understanding and copying. GB is about 5% of revenue. Its App Total New Subs is -12.9% this period.

ios.head: No big App Total Revenue swing expected in about 7 days — the share of installs that become subs is normal.
ios.body: App Total New Subs is -1.9% and App Total Install is -0.6%; the gap between them (-1.3pp) is under the 10pp we treat as a real signal, so the share of people who install and then subscribe is close to normal. New subs start as 7-day free trials, so today's new subs are next period's App Total Revenue. So nothing unusual is building up that would swing App Total Revenue in about 7 days.

ios.head: App Total Revenue is down in every app — something is affecting all of them, not one.
ios.body: App Total Revenue is down in every app (All App -5.5%, YMK -3.2%, YCP -7.7%, YCV -5.7%). When all apps move together the cause is usually something they share — the season, an app-store change, or how the data is collected — rather than any one app's own doing.
